name: WreckLess
shortDescription: Always-on security agent swarm on one Dell GB10: it reads a new advisory, exploits your code, patches it and proves the fix, with every model running locally.
description:
A critical advisory lands for a dependency you use: are you exposed, can you prove it, what's the fix, and does it hold? WreckLess answers all four on a box under your desk, in about a minute, and nothing ships until a human approves.

Highlights:
- Six agents, one job each: Scout finds where the bug lives in your code, Ralph writes a real exploit and fires it in a locked sandbox, Verifier re-runs it on fresh copies, Felix patches the root cause, Conductor ships the fix, and Porter answers questions in Slack.
- No agent grades its own work: the Verifier is plain code, not a model.
- 47–80 s from advisory to validated patch, and 5 / 5 on live replays of a real 2024 CVE (LangChain's VectorSQLDatabaseChain `eval()`).
- 100% local inference: three models (Qwen3-Coder) on vLLM, loopback only, inside an OpenShell sandbox with no outbound network. Zero bytes of your code go to a cloud model.
- Approval comes through a Slack card over an outbound-only airlock and is bound to the exact commit before a draft PR opens.

Built with Dae Jang at the Dell × NVIDIA AI Hackathon in San Francisco.
